FINDING_ID: R4_F001  
SEVERITY: 0.87  
FLAW_CLASS: 5 (correctness)  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.84  
VERIFIED: TRUE  
DESCRIPTION: `DynamicManager.process_round()` updates the live fingerprints only when `not self.fsm.is_terminal`. This means the final executed round of the run is never incorporated into `_live_fingerprints` or `_round_metrics`, even though that round is part of the observed evidence base. This creates a cross-area state inconsistency: `round_results`, convergence, and failure histories include the terminal round, but the adaptive capability state omits it. Any post-run analysis, resumable orchestration, audit, or handoff that inspects “live” capabilities after completion will read stale fingerprints from the previous round rather than the last observed behavior.

FINDING_ID: R4_F002  
SEVERITY: 0.83  
FLAW_CLASS: 1 (logic)  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.81  
VERIFIED: TRUE  
DESCRIPTION: `DynamicManager.process_round()` has no guard against being called after the FSM has already reached `TERMINAL`. The method proceeds to emit events, detect failures, mutate convergence/diminishing-returns state, append a new `RoundResult`, and only then calls `self.fsm.select_event(...)` / `transition(...)`, which will fail because the FSM is terminal. This leaves partial side effects from an illegal extra round and corrupts manager state before the exception is raised. The method should reject terminal-state invocation before any mutations.

FINDING_ID: R4_F003  
SEVERITY: 0.80  
FLAW_CLASS: 2 (interface)  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.79  
VERIFIED: TRUE  
DESCRIPTION: `DynamicManager.check_dispatch_feasibility()` evaluates feasibility against the caller-supplied `ModelSpec` object, not the manager’s current live model state from `get_live_models()`. Because `get_live_models()` is the manager’s authoritative active/live view, this creates an interface split: allocation decisions are based on the manager’s current model set, but feasibility checks can still be run on stale or inactive specs held by the caller. In particular, a caller can ask feasibility for a model that has already been excluded, and the method will still return a normal dispatch decision and emit events against it.

FINDING_ID: R4_F004  
SEVERITY: 0.76  
FLAW_CLASS: 6 (edge-case)  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.72  
VERIFIED: TRUE  
DESCRIPTION: `LoadBalancer.solve()` does not reject the case `models=[]` when `tasks` is non-empty. In that case `_solve_greedy()` builds a `(J, 0)` matrix, `_check_feasibility()` reports all tasks unassigned, and `_objective()` returns a numeric cost despite there being no allocatable models. The method therefore returns an `Allocation` object with zero columns rather than failing fast on an impossible input. This is a distinct impossible-state bug from the previously noted empty-task behavior.

FINDING_ID: R4_F005  
SEVERITY: 0.74  
FLAW_CLASS: 6 (edge-case)  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.70  
VERIFIED: TRUE  
DESCRIPTION: `CorrelatedFailureModel.set_vulnerability()` permits `model_i == model_j`, storing a self-pair key `frozenset({model_i})`. However, `get_vulnerability()` special-cases identical model IDs and always returns `1.0`, so any stored self-vulnerability is ignored forever. This is an inconsistent API contract: the setter accepts a value that the getter can never surface. It should either reject self-pairs or define coherent semantics for them.

FINDING_ID: R4_F006  
SEVERITY: 0.72  
FLAW_CLASS: 1 (logic)  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.77  
VERIFIED: TRUE  
DESCRIPTION: `DynamicManager.process_round()` trusts `responses` and `findings` without enforcing that all observations belong to the manager’s current round. `round_idx` is taken from `self.fsm.current_round`, but each `ModelResponse` and `Finding` also carries its own `round_idx`, and no consistency check is performed. A caller can therefore accidentally submit stale or future-labeled artifacts into the current round, causing cross-round contamination of failure history, convergence classes, diminishing-returns yield, and fingerprint adaptation.

FINDING_ID: R4_F007  
SEVERITY: 0.69  
FLAW_CLASS: 2 (interface)  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.74  
VERIFIED: TRUE  
DESCRIPTION: `DynamicManager.process_round()` accepts `responses` for arbitrary model IDs not present in the configured pool. `FailureHandler.detect_failure()` will process such responses, `_perf_history.setdefault(response.model_id, []).append(perf)` will create ad hoc performance state for unknown IDs, and `failures` will record them, but downstream subsystems such as role assignment, active model tracking, and live fingerprints do not consistently know about these models. This admits out-of-pool identities into part of the state machine and should be rejected at the orchestration boundary.

FINDING_ID: R4_F008  
SEVERITY: 0.67  
FLAW_CLASS: 6 (edge-case)  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.68  
VERIFIED: TRUE  
DESCRIPTION: `DynamicManager.update_fingerprints()` assumes every active model ID exists in `_live_fingerprints`. If a bad state arises where `FailureHandler.active_models` contains an ID not present in the original model set, `old_fp = self._live_fingerprints[model_id]` raises `KeyError`. Because `process_round()` does not validate response/model identities and role/failure maps are mutable dictionaries, this is a real robustness gap in a cross-component boundary.

FINDING_ID: R4_F009  
SEVERITY: 0.63  
FLAW_CLASS: 5 (correctness)  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.71  
VERIFIED: TRUE  
DESCRIPTION: `RoleAssignment.get_ordering()` returns the initially cached `capability_scores` from `assign()` and never recomputes them after `reassign()` or after live fingerprints change. The method name and docstring imply a current ordering `≽_rho`, but in practice it exposes a stale snapshot from initialization. This makes introspection and any downstream consumer of `get_ordering()` semantically wrong once the system has adapted or roles have been reassigned.

FINDING_ID: R4_F010  
SEVERITY: 0.61  
FLAW_CLASS: 6 (edge-case)  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.66  
VERIFIED: TRUE  
DESCRIPTION: `ConvergenceDetector.add_round_findings()` and `DiminishingReturnsDetector.add_round()` accept arbitrary `round_idx` values, including negative indices, and `DynamicManager.process_round()` never asserts non-negativity beyond what the FSM happens to use. A negative round inserted directly into these detectors can invalidate cumulative computations that iterate `for r in range(round_idx + 1)` and produce empty or malformed histories. The public APIs should reject negative round indices explicitly.

Definitive stance: there are still new, non-duplicate issues in the artifact, primarily around illegal-state handling, stale/final-state adaptation, identity/round consistency at orchestration boundaries, and impossible-input acceptance.
